summary:
Israel does not criminalise consensual same-sex conduct. Outright International's country matrix (last updated 12 March 2026) records no criminalisation of same-sex acts in the criminal code alongside some legal protections, while also indicating gaps in the recognition framework. The prevailing assessment of Israel as the most permissive destination in its subregion, with Tel Aviv functioning as a regional queer hub, rests on that legal baseline.

Legal gender recognition runs through the courts. In July 2025 the High Court of Justice blocked a fast-track attempt to undo a person's registered gender change, holding that the 2021 certificate remains valid. Since 2025 the registration of a person's previous name has been abolished for transgender people, so a changed document no longer carries an old-name trace. Attorney General Haim Cohn blocked Rina Natan's sex reassignment surgery in 1954, and legal recognition of sex reassignment was only established in 1986.

Border screening is the sharpest visitor-specific exposure. A first-person account published by Haaretz on 3 May 2023 documents a transgender traveller subjected to gender-identity humiliation at an Israeli airport, with security personnel insisting that without surgery a person remains male. The Israel Police adopted a new regulation governing the searching of transgender people in May 2023, in response to complaints about humiliating searches of trans detainees and travellers.

Recorded anti-LGBTQ violence rose during 2025. Jerusalem Post reporting on 2025 data shows an increase in homophobic and transphobic attacks, and Ynet reports record assault totals, including dating-app traps and organised ambushes that lure victims to attacks. Haaretz reported in February 2025 that inflammatory rhetoric from the United States was affecting Israel's trans community, with trans Israelis describing heightened fear as that discourse spilled into the local climate.

Detention carries a specific risk for trans visitors and residents. Isolation and segregation of transgender prisoners is the documented default management practice rather than placement in facilities matching gender identity, as a law-journal study in the Buffalo Gender and Law Journal records. In October 2019 an Israeli court ordered the Israel Prison Service to provide hormone-replacement therapy to a trans woman prisoner and to transfer her from a men's prison to a women's prison after a petition by ACRI; she was initially held in a separate wing of the women's prison, and ACRI prepared a further petition seeking her placement with the general population, showing that placement is decided case by case and that trans women have at times been held in men's prisons.

Care and partnership protections exist in parts. A directive issued by Health Minister Nitzan Horowitz on 14 February 2022 banned licensed medical professionals from conducting conversion therapy, though it does not bind clergy or alternative practitioners and has not been codified by the Knesset; the governing coalition defeated a bill to ban conversion therapy on 24 February 2016. In December 2016 Attorney General Avichai Mandelblit instructed the Interior Ministry to extend the same citizenship rights to same-sex couples as to opposite-sex couples, after same-sex spouses had previously waited up to seven years and typically received only permanent residency; a December 2004 Tel Aviv District Court ruling extended a 1999 Supreme Court rule barring deportation of foreign nationals married to Israeli citizens to common-law and same-sex couples.
tangentialFactors:
Public visibility and organised resistance have a long record: Israel's first LGBT pride march was held on 17 September 1977, Tel Aviv's first Pride parade in 1993, and Eilat Pride began in 2001. Jerusalem Pride was initially banned by municipal order until a court overturned the ban; the 2005 march was attacked by Yishai Schlissel, who stabbed three people and received a ten-year sentence, and after his 2015 release he stabbed six marchers and killed teenage girl Shira Banki. The 2018 Aguda-organised LGBTQ strike drew over 100,000 people to a Tel Aviv rally, and an estimated 250,000 marched in Tel Aviv Pride in June 2022.

Events are exposed to security conditions as well as to attack. The 2025 Tel Aviv Pride on 13 June was cancelled by the municipality after Israeli strikes on Iranian targets. In 2026 the Jerusalem Municipality raised the Pride flag for the first time along the route from Sacher Park to the Knesset, with flags carrying the Hebrew inscription "equality in life" hung along the parade route. The Jerusalem Open House staged the 21 June 2007 Jerusalem parade after police allocated thousands of personnel to secure the area, and a central Jerusalem square is to be renamed "Tolerance Square" in memory of Shira Banki.

Armed attack has targeted community infrastructure: on 1 August 2009 an attacker killed two people and injured 15 at a lesbian and gay centre in Tel Aviv, condemned by Prime Minister Netanyahu and President Peres. Public support for same-sex marriage runs ahead of legislative positions, with a Channel 10 survey finding majority backing while half of MKs declined to state a position.

Historical context: under the British Mandate official questionnaires documented "unnatural" sexual expression, including sodomy between school boys, and Britain pushed criminalisation into Palestinian schools and society, a policy carried into the Israeli state. In 1943 the Acre district court tried Mustafa Naif, aged 16, alongside Mustafa Zaharan for sodomy; Naif recanted to protect his friend, was convicted of perjury instead, and faced a sodomy charge carrying up to 10 years' imprisonment.
localsOnly:
Family formation remains constrained for residents. A July 2018 surrogacy law excluded single men and same-sex couples, and the Knesset voted in July 2018 to keep them out of surrogacy; the High Court of Justice ruled on 27 February 2020 and the Supreme Court unanimously on 11 July 2021 that the ban violated equality and the right to parenthood, effective 12 January 2022. Between 2008 and 2017 only 3 of 550 same-sex couples seeking to adopt succeeded, against more than a thousand heterosexual couples, until the government reversed course in August 2017 under Supreme Court pressure.

Conversion-therapy regulation reaches licensed practitioners only. The 14 February 2022 Health Ministry directive binds psychologists, social workers and Ministry of Health-licensed therapists, but not rabbis, clergy or alternative practitioners, and the Knesset has not codified it into law. On 24 February 2016 the governing coalition defeated both a bill to ban conversion therapy and a bill to train health professionals on gender and sexual orientation issues.

Community infrastructure includes the Municipal LGBT Community Center opened by the City of Tel Aviv in 2008, the first of its kind in the country, and the Jerusalem Open House. Outright International's March 2026 matrix states that LGBTI organisations in Israel cannot register.

Access to transition care has been historically contested: Attorney General Haim Cohn blocked Rina Natan's sex reassignment surgery in 1954, and legal recognition of sex reassignment came only in 1986; the October 2019 court order requiring hormone-replacement therapy for a trans woman prisoner shows that court intervention has been needed to secure transition treatment in custody.
outOfScopeNotes:
Sources conflict on legal gender recognition. Outright International's country page, last updated 12 March 2026, states that there is no legal gender recognition, while Jerusalem Post reporting describes abolition of previous-name registration for transgender people in 2025 and the July 2025 High Court of Justice ruling treats a 2021 gender-change certificate as remaining valid. The scope, qualifying conditions and procedural route of recognition in each account are not resolved in the available material, and the two accounts may be describing different aspects of the process.

A source at legalclarity.org addressing trans rights in Israel, covering laws, protections and gaps, returned HTTP 404 at research time, so its content could not be verified or used.

Whether the Israel Police search regulation of May 2023 has been enforced as written, or how often border screening of the kind described in the May 2023 Haaretz account still occurs, is not established by the sources here. The 2025 rise in anti-LGBTQ violence is reported from official data, but the figures for trans victims specifically are not broken down in the material available.

Outright International's statement that LGBTI organisations cannot register is not corroborated by another source in the inventory, and the practical effect for visitors or for local advocacy is not sourced.
